messages:
maria_ops: Heads up — seeing a sudden burst of GPU evictions in eu-west1 core-pool. 3 eviction events in the last 2m, scheduler is redistributing and latency is climbing for some customers. Not a full outage yet but trending bad.
jonathan_infra: I can confirm. Node eviction logs show NVML resets + OCI oom signals. Autoscaler didn't trigger because node-level healthy checks passed.
zoe_oncall: Marking as incident, moving to P1. Creating incident room and notifying oncall rotation.
sre-bot: Alert: region eu-west1 GPU_eviction_rate = 0.78%/min, avg token latency +220ms, queue depth increased 18%. Recommend temporary rate-shearing and per-tenant soft-quotas per runbook-eviction-mitigation.
kai_eng: Can we apply per-customer QPS caps quickly? We should protect SLA tenants and shed noisy tenants first. Suggest: SLA-tier allowed, reserved-dedicated unaffected, everything else get adaptive softcap at 50% of normal sustained QPS.
jonathan_infra: I can push softcap policy now via infra-control: ``rctl apply --scope region:eu-west1 --policy adaptive_softcap --levels non-sla=50%,free=40%``. Will stage to canary pool then global.
maria_ops: Also start moving low-priority batch jobs off eu-west1 to eu-central and us-east to free up GPUs — luke_platform can we trigger migration?
luke_platform: Starting migration of batch workload set `bw-spot-06` to eu-central. ETA ~7m. I'll also disable autoscaler scale-down to avoid churn during migrations.
alina_support: Notifying impacted customers: we'll message non-SLA customers hitting 429s. SLA customers get a heads-up that we're enforcing temporary caps to preserve latency. Drafted a short blurb for status page.
sre-bot: Runbook step 3 initiated: apply per-tenant adaptive caps, drain non-critical pods, migrate batches. Logging actions to incident ticket #INC-1933.
ops-runbook-bot: Playbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/eviction-mitigation — step executed: softcap policy applied to 15% of traffic as canary. Monitor for backend queue recovery.
zoe_oncall: Canary results: token latency for canary slices down ~60ms within 90s. Eviction rate on canary nodes dropped to 0.12%/min. Proceed to roll to remaining pools?
kai_eng: Proceed. Also bump KV cache retention for in-flight sessions in eu-west1 to reduce rework. Adding `--kv-cache-ttl=30s` to runtime config for affected pools.
jonathan_infra: Rolling softcap to all pools now. Command output: ``policy applied: eu-west1 {non-sla:50%,free:40%} — distributed to 32 nodes``.
maria_ops: Observed immediate queue reduction, but still seeing some noisy tenants exceeding caps via retries. Need per-tenant retry-backoff enforcement in gateway.
luke_platform: Enabled retry-backoff enforcement at edge gateway for eu-west1: `retry_limit=2, backoff=500ms->2s` for non-SLA.
alina_support: Status page updated: "Degraded capacity in EU-West1 causing temporary rate limits for non-SLA customers. We've applied adaptive caps and are migrating batch workloads. Expect recovery in 20-40m." Posting to customers now. :loudspeaker:
zoe_oncall: Monitoring — eviction rate down to 0.05%/min, region GPU utilization normalizing ~82%. Keeping incident open for another 30m observation.
sre-bot: Auto follow-up scheduled in 30m. If eviction rate <0.1%/min and latency stable, recommend rollback softcaps to 80% in next window.
kai_eng: We'll keep the KV tweak for 10m then revert. Documenting exact confs in the incident ticket.
maria_ops: Post-incident actions: 1) investigate cause — noisy tenant or kernel regression; 2) run mixed workload replay against staging with same kernel bits; 3) follow up on autoscaler logic so node-level passes don't prevent fleet-scale reaction.
alina_support: I logged impacted customers and created follow-ups with account teams.
zoe_oncall: Closing loop — we'll mark as 'mitigated' once all rolling actions complete. Thanks everyone for fast moves. :thumbsup:
